items.claim: The close at 5:24/5:25 is argued without two facts of the Aramaic that bear on it. First, oshb:Dan.5.24 opens on the then-connective, which the device inventory lists at this verse and the row does not name; with it the speech leaves the second-person charge of 5:22-5:23 for a third-person report of the hand and the writing. Second, the last three words of oshb:Dan.5.24 are taken up, reordered, by the first four words of oshb:Dan.5.25, which opens with the conjunction; the row's cut falls between the two halves of that repetition. The row's mark, count and quotation facts are otherwise true, and no mark follows 5:23 or 5:24.
items.both_sides: Near side (5:24): opens on the then-connective, shifts from address to report, and ends on the words for this writing inscribed. Far side (5:25): opens with the conjunction and the same three lexemes, then gives the inscription; 5:26 opens the listed interpretation formula. So 5:24 looks both ways: it closes the indictment by naming its consequence and it introduces the writing that 5:25 reads. A cut after 5:23 would put the connective at a unit head and keep the repetition whole; the cut after 5:24 keeps cause and consequence together. No mark decides it. This weighing is INFERRED; the row's medium-low grade and its live rival are right, and I propose no move of the cut, only that the rationale weigh the seam with these facts and name the cut after 5:23 as a rival.
